title: Spoiled Tiffin

items.label: Morning Packing
items.description: A Bangladeshi parent packs rice and vegetable curry into a reusable steel tiffin box before a Rajshahi student leaves home.

questions: Which two scenes show what the heat costs the student?
When has packed food become unappealing before you could eat it?
Is food waste or the extra lunch expense the bigger problem?
Why might a lunch bag become hot before noon?
If a student skips the spoiled meal, what problem follows?
What could you try in 7 days for at most 1,500 BDT? Who might pay if it worked?

starter_experiment.pilot: Ask ten students or workers how they carry lunch, how long it stays warm, and how often food must be discarded; use a food thermometer if available.
starter_experiment.potential_customer: Students, workers, households, or food sellers
starter_experiment.test_metric: Time without cooling, discarded meals, and replacement-lunch costs
starter_experiment.note: Optional cash ceiling for a first experiment, not money required to begin or a full launch budget. Start with tools and relationships already available; pay partners fairly and account for founder time before scaling.

evidence.editor_note: The sources establish food-safety risk in high heat and Rajshahi heat conditions. The tiffin story is an illustrative student scenario; it does not diagnose spoilage from smell alone.
